title.en: How could Reform UK spend its £72m of new billionaire donations?
title.zh: 英国改革党如何花费其7200万英镑的新亿万富翁捐款？

summary.en: Reform UK has received substantial donations totaling £72 million from billionaires Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo. This influx of cash could provide a significant advantage in an election campaign, but the party must navigate potential pitfalls associated with large, unconditional funding.
summary.zh: 英国改革党（Reform UK）收到了来自亿万富翁克里斯托弗·哈伯恩（Christopher Harborne）和本·德洛（Ben Delo）共计7200万英镑的巨额捐款。这笔资金的涌入可能为竞选活动提供巨大的优势，但该党必须谨慎处理与巨额、无条件资金相关的潜在风险。

body.en: Harborne and Delo’s cash could buy a massive head start in an election, but spending big has possible pitfalls Nigel Farage once said he could spend his £5m gift from Christopher Harborne on Ferraris if he wanted to, given its unconditional nature. With the new donations to his party from Harborne and his fellow crypto billionaire Ben Delo of £72m over the past weekend alone, Farage’s party now has nearly enough cash to buy a Reform UK branded Ferrari for a party organiser in each of Britain’s 632 constituencies (though that would certainly be a waste and a bit of a tax headache). Continue reading...
body.zh: 哈伯尼和德洛的现金可以在选举中获得巨大的领先优势，但花大钱可能会陷入陷阱。奈杰尔·法拉奇曾表示，如果他愿意，他可以将克里斯托弗·哈伯尼的 500 万英镑礼物花在法拉利上，因为它是无条件的。仅在上周末，Harborne 和他的加密货币亿万富翁 Ben Delo 就向他的政党捐赠了 7200 万英镑，Farage 的政党现在几乎有足够的现金为英国 632 个选区的政党组织者购买一辆 Reform UK 品牌的法拉利（尽管这肯定会造成浪费，而且会带来一些税收问题）。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The influx of £72 million into Reform UK's coffers presents a significant opportunity for the party, but also a profound ethical challenge. Micah 6:8 calls us to 'act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.' The question for the party, and indeed for all political actors, is how this wealth will be stewarded – will it serve the public...
reflection.zh: 英国改革党（Reform UK）获得7200万英镑的巨额捐款，这为该党带来了巨大的机遇，但也伴随着严峻的道德挑战。弥迦书6章8节呼吁我们“行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的雅伟同行”。对于该党，乃至所有政治参与者而言，关键问题是如何管理这笔财富——它将以正直服务于公众利益，还是沦为谋取私利的工具？

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Sweden general election: close race as far right eyes role in government – Europe live
title.zh: 瑞典大选：极右翼寻求执政角色，选情胶着

summary.en: Sweden is holding parliamentary elections with the latest polls showing a very narrow 0.3-point gap between the left-wing and right-wing blocs. The far-right Sweden Democrats are hoping to play a significant role in the next government.
summary.zh: 瑞典正举行议会选举，最新民调显示左翼和右翼集团之间的差距仅为0.3个百分点。极右翼瑞典民主党希望在下一届政府中扮演重要角色。

body.en: Hej , that’s hello in Swedish, from Stockholm, where I spent this morning eating Swedish pastry and meatballs talking to voters about the country’s prospects as they cast their votes in today’s parliamentary elections.
body.zh: Hej，瑞典语中的“你好”，来自斯德哥尔摩，今天早上我在那里吃着瑞典糕点和肉丸，与在今天的议会选举中投票的选民谈论该国的前景。

reflection.en: As Sweden navigates a closely contested election, the outcome will shape the nation's direction. The possibility of the far-right gaining influence raises questions about the kind of leadership that will guide the country. Proverbs 29:2 reminds us that the character of leaders profoundly impacts a nation's well-being, urging a prayer for wisdom and...
reflection.zh: 随着瑞典经历一场竞争激烈的选举，其结果将塑造国家的发展方向。极右翼可能获得影响力的可能性，引发了关于何种领导层将引导国家的疑问。《箴言》29章2节提醒我们，领导者的品格对国家的福祉有着深远的影响，促使我们为治理的智慧和公义祈祷。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: Kamala Harris’s California home targeted by trespasser, officials say
title.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯在加州的住所被闯入者侵入，官员称

summary.en: Officials stated that a trespasser was stopped at the Malibu home of former Vice President Kamala Harris and her husband on Friday night. Neither Harris nor her husband were present at the time, and no arrests were made. Security personnel intercepted the individual before they reached the residence.
summary.zh: 官员称，周五晚间，前副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯及其丈夫位于马里布的住所发生闯入事件，一名闯入者被阻止。哈里斯和她的丈夫当时都不在家，未有人被逮捕。安保人员在闯入者到达住宅前将其截获。

body.en:
Law enforcement officials and a spokesperson for former vice-president Kamala Harris said a trespasser was stopped at her Malibu home in California on Friday night.

Neither the former vice-president nor her husband, Doug Emhoff, were home at the time.

“Security personnel stopped an individual who illegally entered Vice-President Harris and Second Gentleman Emhoff’s property before the individual reached the home,” Harris spokesperson Eduardo Negrón said in a statement on Saturday, reported by Politico . “Vice-President Harris and Second Gentleman Emhoff were not present. They are grateful to the security and law enforcement personnel who responded swiftly.”

Malibu Lost Hills sheriff’s deputies responded to Harris’s home around 10.30pm that Friday night on a report of a “suspicious person”, according to a statement from the Los Angeles county sheriff’s department, after private security had stopped the individual.

“The individual who was outside of the property upon our arrival was warned and advised by deputies to leave the premises and left voluntarily without incident,” the sheriff’s department said in a statement. “A trespassing report was taken. Sheriff’s Malibu Lost Hills Deputies will increase patrols in the area as a precaution.”

Vice-presidents in the US typically receive six months of Secret Service protection after leaving office. Former president Joe Biden extended Harris’s security detail to 18 months before leaving office. That extension was canceled in August 2025 by Donald Trump. Ex-presidents typically receive security protection for life.

Harris bought the home in the Point Dume area of Malibu for $8.1m this May , which prompted speculation that she would not run for president again. The celebrity studded retreat is typically seen as a place where people “ downshift ”, according to a Politico article at the time.
body.zh: 执法官员和前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯的发言人表示，周五晚上，一名侵入者在她位于加利福尼亚州马里布的家中被拦住。 当时，前副总统和她的丈夫道格·埃姆霍夫都不在家。 据 Politico 报道，哈里斯发言人爱德华多·内格隆 (Eduardo Negrón) 在周六的一份声明中表示，“安全人员在一名非法进入副总统哈里斯和埃姆霍夫二绅士的住所之前将其拦住。” “哈里斯副总统和埃姆霍夫二等人没有在场。他们感谢迅速反应的安全和执法人员。” 根据洛杉矶县治安部门的一份声明，在私人保安拦下该人后，马里布失落山警长的副手于周五晚上 10 点 30 分左右赶到哈里斯的家，接到“可疑人员”的报告。 警长部门在一份声明中表示：“我们到达时，在该物业外的人已被警员警告并建议离开该物业，并自愿离开，没有发生任何事件。” “已收到非法侵入报告。作为预防措施，马里布失落山治安官将增加该地区的巡逻。” 美国副总统在卸任后通常会受到特勤局六个月的保护。前总统乔·拜登在离任前将哈里斯的安保期限延长至 18 个月。唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 于 2025 年 8 月取消了这一延期。前总统通常会获得终身安全保护。 哈里斯今年 5 月以 810 万美元的价格购买了马里布 Point Dume 地区的房屋，这引发了人们对她不会再次竞选总统的猜测。据《Politico》当时的一篇文章称，这个名人云集的度假胜地通常被视为人们“放慢生活节奏”的地方。

reflection.en: The news of a trespasser on a private property, even when the residents are unharmed, highlights the importance of boundaries and the rule of law. The Apostle Paul reminds us in Romans 13:1 that governing authorities are established by Yahweh, and respecting these structures is part of living in an ordered society. This incident, while thankfully without...
reflection.zh: 一名闯入者进入私人住宅的消息，即使居民安然无恙，也凸显了界限和法治的重要性。使徒保罗在罗马书13:1提醒我们，在位的掌权者是雅伟所立的，尊重这些结构是我们有序生活的一部分。这起事件虽然庆幸没有造成进一步的伤害，但却强调了保护我们的家园和社区所需的警惕和制度。

verse.textEn: Let everyone be subject to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which God has established.
verse.textZh: 在上有权柄的，人人当顺服他，因为没有权柄不是出于神的。

title.en: Trump reiterates $5,000 ‘dividend’ pledge if Republicans win midterms
title.zh: 特朗普重申共和党若赢得中期选举将发放5000美元“红利”的承诺

summary.en: Donald Trump has reiterated his controversial pledge to give US adults a $5,000 "dividend" if Republicans retain control of Congress after the upcoming midterm elections. This plan, which could cost over a trillion dollars, has been met with widespread incredulity and accusations of attempting to bribe voters,...
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普重申了他一项备受争议的承诺，即如果共和党在中期选举后继续控制国会，将向美国成年人发放5000美元的“红利”。这项可能耗资超过万亿美元的计划，在美国国家债务已于8月首次突破40万亿美元之际，已引发了广泛的难以置信和贿赂选民的指控。

body.en: Plan to give US adults $5,000 has been greeted with incredulity across the political spectrum as well as outrage Donald Trump on Sunday doubled down on his controversial pledge to give US adults a $5,000 “dividend” if his Republican ⁠party keeps control of Congress after November’s midterm elections. The plan has been greeted with expressions of incredulity across the US political spectrum as well as outraged accusations of seeing to bribe voters. The plan – which would cost more than a trillion dollars – also comes amid huge concern over the US national debt, which topped $40tn for the first time in August. Reuters contributed to this article Continue reading...
body.zh: 向美国成年人发放 5,000 美元的计划遭到了整个政治派别的怀疑和愤怒，唐纳德·特朗普周日加倍强调了他有争议的承诺，如果他的共和党在 11 月中期选举后继续控制国会，他将向美国成年人提供 5,000 美元的“红利”。该计划遭到了美国政界的质疑，并遭到了贿赂选民的愤怒指控。该计划的成本将超过一万亿美元，同时也正值人们对美国国债的巨大担忧之际，美国国债在 8 月份首次突破 40 兆美元。路透社对本文做出了贡献 继续阅读...

reflection.en: The promise of a $5,000 "dividend" to every adult American, if Republicans win the midterms, has sparked controversy. Such pledges, especially when they carry immense financial implications and are perceived as attempts to sway voters, raise questions about the integrity of political promises. Proverbs 11:1 reminds us that dishonest practices are detestable...
reflection.zh: 如果共和党在中期选举中获胜，向每位美国成年人发放5000美元“红利”的承诺引发了争议。此类承诺，尤其是在涉及巨额财政影响并被视为试图影响选民时，会引发对政治承诺诚信的质疑。《箴言》11:1提醒我们，雅伟憎恶不公平的交易，促使人们思考政治提案的伦理层面。

verse.textEn: Yahweh detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him.
verse.textZh: 诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶；公平的法码为他所喜悦。

title.en: AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC
title.zh: 前Anthropic研究员告诉BBC：人工智能员工“真心害怕”人类的未来

summary.en: An AI researcher who quit Anthropic told the BBC that people working on the technology are "genuinely frightened" about the speed of its advancements and what it could mean for humanity.
summary.zh: 一位从Anthropic辞职的人工智能研究员告诉BBC，从事这项技术的人们对它的快速发展及其对人类的潜在影响“真心感到恐惧”。

body.en:
An artificial intelligence researcher who quit AI firm Anthropic has said people working on the technology were "genuinely frightened" about the speed of its advancements and what it could mean for humanity.

"I believe that if we don't slow down at the current rate of progress, there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future," he said.

Jacob Coxon was speaking to the BBC after his resignation post on the dangers of AI went viral on a backdrop of growing safety concerns about the industry.

The 27-year-old's former boss, Anthropic head Dario Amodei, recently called for AI development to slow down - though some have questioned the motivations behind this.

The bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk of xAI, have both said they agree with Amodei's proposal for industry-wide deceleration and regulation, as well as independent monitoring of AI model development.

Amodei wrote in an essay on Saturday that developing the technology was not in question, but the risks associated with it were "serious", and that companies and governments must be given time to address them.

Coxon – who worked at OpenAI before joining Anthropic – welcomed the suggestion of a slowdown but said it would need to be co-ordinated with China to avoid "a race at an international scale".

"The people who work at these companies are completely serious when they ask for regulation because they find themselves trapped in a race. And they're scared of the outcomes of that race," he told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg.

The hardest question to answer, according to Coxon, was what an AI apocalypse would look like.

One of the risks outlined in Amodei's comments was of a swarm of bots acting like a supercomputer that could take over the internet.

In response to Coxon's departure, an Anthropic spokesperson told BBC News: "We have always been transparent that AI will bring both enormous benefits and unprecedented risks.

"To address these risks, we continue to build models with some of the strongest safeguards in the industry."

The firm has been a pioneer in studying how AI models work, the spokesperson added. It was the first to publish a framework for mitigating the risks posed by their development - and it also "aggressively" tests its models and publishes the findings to aid scrutiny and prevent incidents of "AI misalignment".

"This work is also why we believe the world would benefit from the industry adopting a lawful, verifiable way to work together to pace how we release powerful models," they said.

He said staff at AI firms were "planning what to do with their lives and thinking about the impacts of their work", while some were "considering buying land somewhere because they're so scared of the instability as a result of rapid AI...
body.zh: 一位退出 Anthropic 的人工智能研究人员告诉 BBC，从事这项技术的人们“真的害怕”它的进步速度以及它对人类的意义。 周六，雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 接受了英国广播公司 (BBC) 的劳拉·昆斯伯格 (Laura Kuenssberg) 采访，谈论了他的病毒式辞职帖子，他在帖子中提出了对人工智能失控的担忧。 “我相信，如果我们不按照目前的进展速度放慢速度，我们很有可能在不久的将来都会死去，”他说。 他辞职之际，该行业的安全担忧日益严重，其中包括他的前老板、Anthropic 公司负责人达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei)，他在周六的一篇文章中主张放慢发展速度。 然而，一些行业人士表示，这种危险被夸大了，可能是为了在这两家最大的人工智能公司潜在上市之前进行炒作，或者是为了促进监管，从而减缓其竞争对手的步伐。 27 岁的英国人 Coxon 的研究重点是训练人工智能模型，他表示，包括埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 OpenAI 的萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 在内的人工智能领导者也与阿莫迪有着类似的担忧。 “他们都发表了关于必须警惕人工智能接管的可能性的声明。他们都谈到了这一点。人工智能接管意味着人类灭绝，”考克森说。 考克森表示，最难回答的问题是它会是什么样子。 考克森说：“你可以提出的任何具体场景最终听起来都像科幻小说。”但他指出，已经发生的进步在过去听起来就像小说。 考克森说，一种潜在的情况可能是人工智能代理侵入医学实验室，“自主生产致命病毒”。他列出的另一个例子可能是人工智能入侵“世界运行的关键基础设施”。 研究人员指出 OpenAI 最近的一份报告，该报告详细介绍了其自己的技术如何对名为 Hugging Face 的在线平台进行黑客攻击。 考克森说：“他们是自主完成的，没有任何人为鼓励。他们选择继续这种黑客热潮。事情变得越来越快，事情也变得越来越可怕。” 阿莫迪的评论中概述的风险之一是一群机器人像超级计算机一样可以接管互联网。 据报道，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 正在为可能创纪录的首次公开募股做准备。行业人士表示，有关人工智能的危险和力量的评论可能旨在引起炒作。其他批评者表示，Anthropic 一直试图引发监管推动阻止竞争，使其和 OpenAI 形成双寡头垄断。 Coxon的观点也遭到了AI平台Hugging Face首席执行官Clement Delangue的质疑。 “抱歉，但是向雅各布询问人工智能......

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of AI, as described by a former Anthropic researcher, raises profound questions about human ambition and foresight. The biblical story of Babel warns against unchecked human endeavors that, while seemingly unified and powerful, can lead to unintended and chaotic consequences when divorced from divine wisdom. This echoes the fear that...
reflection.zh: 正如一位前Anthropic研究员所描述的，人工智能的飞速发展引发了关于人类野心和远见的深刻问题。圣经中关于巴别塔的故事告诫人们，那些看似统一而强大的、不受约束的人类努力，如果脱离了神的智慧，可能会导致意想不到的混乱后果。这与人们对人工智能不受控制的进步可能超越我们明智引导能力，从而带来生存风险的恐惧不谋而合。

verse.textEn: Yahweh said, 'If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.'
verse.textZh: 雅伟说：「看哪，他们成为一样的人民，都是一样的言语，如今既做起这事来，以后他们所要做的事就没有不成就的了。」

title.en: Turkish police detain dozens in raids on gay bars and homes of LGBTQ+ activists
title.zh: 土耳其警方突袭同性恋酒吧和LGBTQ+活动人士住所，拘留数十人

summary.en: Police in Turkey have detained 47 people in raids targeting gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ+ activists. Human rights groups accuse the government of using a 'My Family is Safe' campaign, ostensibly to protect family values, as a pretext to target the LGBTQ+ community.
summary.zh: 土耳其警方在一系列突袭同性恋酒吧和LGBTQ+活动人士住所的行动中拘留了47人。人权组织指责政府利用名为“我的家庭安全”的宣传活动，表面上是为了保护家庭价值观，但实际上是借口针对LGBTQ+社群。

body.en:
Police in Turkey have detained 47 people in a series of raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ+ activists, officials say.

Raids took place in 12 provinces over the weekend as part of a campaign dubbed "My Family is Safe" that the Turkish government says has been designed to protect family values.

Same-sex marriage is not recognised in Turkey, with growing pressure on gay couples. Human rights groups in Turkey have accused the government of using the campaign to target the LGBTQ+ community.

Officers detained 26 people and seized drugs, digital equipment, smuggled alcohol and a firearm during the raids, according to the Istanbul chief prosecutor's office.

In a separate statement, the Ankara chief prosecutor's office said another 21 people had been detained as part of an investigation into Kaos GL.

The organisation said 50 activists had been detained, more than 10 taken after police raids on their homes.

It said that authorities had blocked several websites and social media accounts linked to LGBTQ+ organisations.

According to the group, authorities have accused Kaos GL of making "obscenity" in online posts that are available to children and had demanded the shutting down of the Kaos GL X account, as well as those of around 15 other LGBTQ+ organisations.

Same-sex relations are not an offence in Turkey but homophobia is common, with President Recep Tayyip Erdogan describing LGBTQ people as "perverts" responsible for the falling birth rate.

As part of "My Family is Safe", Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek says legal proceedings have been started against more than 160 people and a number of organisations and companies across the country.

Gurlek did not say how many people had been taken into custody, but said the raids came in the context of the "Decade of the Family" campaign.

However, the Turkish Human Rights Association says the Turkish government has been using the campaign to target the LGBTQ+ community in recent years.

"The real name of this operation is not 'My Family is Safe'; it is state-led discrimination, politics of fear and the dismantling of civil society," the organisation said on X.
body.zh: 官员称，土耳其警方对同性恋酒吧和 LGBTQ+ 活动人士的住宅进行了一系列突击搜查，拘留了 47 人。 周末，突袭行动在 12 个省份展开，这是“我的家人安全”运动的一部分，土耳其政府称该运动旨在保护家庭价值观。 土耳其不承认同性婚姻，同性恋伴侣面临的压力越来越大。土耳其的人权组织指责政府利用该运动针对 LGBTQ+ 群体。 据伊斯坦布尔首席检察官办公室称，警方在突袭行动中拘留了 26 人，并缴获了毒品、数字设备、走私酒精和枪支。 安卡拉首席检察官办公室在另一份声明中表示，作为对 Kaos GL 调查的一部分，另有 21 人被拘留。 该组织表示，50 名活动人士已被拘留，其中 10 多人是在警方突击搜查他们的住所后被带走的。 据称，当局封锁了多个与 LGBTQ+ 组织相关的网站和社交媒体账户。 据该组织称，当局指控 Kaos GL 在儿童可以看到的在线帖子中发布“淫秽”内容，并要求关闭 Kaos GL X 帐户以及其他约 15 个 LGBTQ+ 组织的帐户。 在土耳其，同性关系并不违法，但恐同现象很普遍，总统雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安 (Recep Tayyip Erdogan) 将 LGBTQ 人群描述为导致出生率下降的“变态”。 土耳其司法部长阿金·古尔莱克 (Akin Gurlek) 表示，作为“我的家人安全”计划的一部分，已经针对全国各地的 160 多人以及一些组织和公司启动了法律诉讼。 古尔莱克没有透露有多少人被拘留，但表示这次突袭是在“家庭十年”运动的背景下进行的。 然而，土耳其人权协会表示，土耳其政府近年来一直利用该运动来针对 LGBTQ+ 群体。 该组织在 X 上表示：“这次行动的真正名称不是‘我的家人安全’；而是国家主导的歧视、恐惧政治和公民社会的瓦解。”

reflection.en: In Turkey, authorities have detained dozens of individuals in raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ+ activists, citing a campaign to protect 'family values.' This action raises concerns among human rights groups who see it as a targeted suppression of the LGBTQ+ community. The call to 'speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves' from Proverbs...
reflection.zh: 在土耳其，当局以保护“家庭价值观”为由，突袭同性恋酒吧并拘留了LGBTQ+活动人士，导致数十人被捕。此举引起了人权组织的担忧，他们认为这是对LGBTQ+社群的压制。《箴言》31:8-9呼吁“要为不能自辩的开口，为所有孤苦者伸明正义”，这在此刻显得尤为重要，提醒我们关注那些面临压力的群体，并为他们的尊严和权利发声。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Legendary Canadian boxer George Chuvalo dies aged 89
title.zh: 传奇加拿大拳击手乔治·楚瓦洛去世，享年89岁

summary.en: George Chuvalo, a Canadian heavyweight boxing champion known for his resilience and never being knocked down, has passed away at the age of 89. He competed against legendary figures like Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier.
summary.zh: 加拿大重量级拳击冠军乔治·楚瓦洛（George Chuvalo）去世，享年89岁。他以其顽强的生命力和从未被击倒的纪录而闻名，曾与穆罕默德·阿里和乔·弗雷泽等传奇人物交锋。

body.en:
Canadian boxer George Chuvalo, a five-time national heavyweight champion, has died at the age of 89.

Out of 93 total professional fights in his career - 73 victories, 18 losses, and two draws - Chuvalo was never once knocked down to the canvas.

"His photos have hung on our walls for decades. His stories have been passed down from one generation of fighters to the next," said Sully's Boxing, the Toronto gym where he trained, in a statement.

He battled Muhammad Ali in 1966 and 1972, and though Chuvalo lost both fights, Ali called him the toughest guy he ever fought.

Chuvalo was born in 1937 to Croatian immigrant parents, grew up in Toronto and got into boxing at a young age.

Widely considered "Canada's greatest warrior", Chuvalo was known for his iron chin, relentless durability, and fights against world famous fighters like George Foreman, Joe Frazier, and Ali.

"George Chuvalo was a heavyweight boxing legend, a family friend and a Canadian icon," Ontario Premier Doug Ford wrote on social media.

"My thoughts are with all of George's family and loved ones as we mourn his passing."

After retiring from professional boxing in 1978, Chuvalo travelled the country as a public speaker advocating for anti-drug education and mental health awareness.

Chuvalo lost three sons and his wife to drug overdoses and suicide, he has said.

"I'd like to think if you're ever tempted with the idea of doing drugs, or you ever flirt with doing drugs, I hope you think of me, George Chuvalo, and what drugs did to my family," he once said, according to a CBC Radio report in 1998.

In retirement, Chuvalo also dipped his toes in acting, appearing in the 1998 comedy film Dirty Work and alongside Jeff Goldblum in the 1986 horror film The Fly.

He also served as a guest commentator for major boxing matches and co-hosted a TV boxing program called Greatest Knockouts with his friend and fellow fighter Charles "Spider" Jones.

Chuvalo is survived by his eldest son Mitch, daughter Vanessa, grandchildren, and second wife Joanne.

Muhammad Ali: 'Why is everything white?' Video, 00:02:40 Muhammad Ali: 'Why is everything white?'
body.zh: 五届全国重量级拳王、加拿大拳击手乔治·丘瓦洛 (George Chuvalo) 去世，享年 89 岁。 在他职业生涯的 93 场职业比赛中——73 场胜利、18 场失败、2 场平局——楚瓦洛从未被击倒在地。 “他的照片已经挂在我们的墙上几十年了。他的故事已经一代一代地流传下去，”他训练的多伦多拳击馆 Sully's Boxing 在一份声明中说。 他在 1966 年和 1972 年与穆罕默德·阿里交手，尽管楚瓦洛两次都输掉了比赛，但阿里称他是他打过的最坚强的人。 丘瓦洛出生于 1937 年，父母是克罗地亚移民，在多伦多长大，很小的时候就开始接触拳击。 楚瓦洛被广泛认为是“加拿大最伟大的战士”，以其铁下巴、顽强的耐力而闻名，并与乔治·福尔曼、乔·弗雷泽和阿里等世界著名拳击手作战。 安大略省省长道格·福特在社交媒体上写道：“乔治·丘瓦洛是重量级拳击传奇人物、家庭朋友和加拿大偶像。” “当我们哀悼乔治的去世时，我的思绪与乔治的所有家人和亲人同在。” 1978 年从职业拳击界退役后，楚瓦洛以公共演讲者的身份周游全国，倡导禁毒教育和心理健康意识。 楚瓦洛表示，他因吸毒过量和自杀而失去了三个儿子和妻子。 据 CBC 广播电台 1998 年的报道，他曾经说过：“我想，如果你曾经想过吸毒，或者你曾经想过吸毒，我希望你能想到我，乔治·丘瓦洛，以及毒品对我的家人造成的影响。” 退休后，楚瓦洛还涉足演艺事业，出演了 1998 年的喜剧电影《肮脏的工作》，并与杰夫·高布伦一起出演了 1986 年的恐怖电影《苍蝇》。 他还担任重大拳击比赛的客座评论员，并与他的朋友兼拳手查尔斯·“蜘蛛”·琼斯共同主持了名为“最伟大的淘汰赛”的电视拳击节目。 楚瓦洛身后留下了长子米奇、女儿凡妮莎、孙子们和第二任妻子乔安妮。 穆罕默德·阿里：“为什么一切都是白色的？”视频，00:02:40 穆罕默德·阿里：“为什么一切都是白色的？”

reflection.en: George Chuvalo's passing at 89 marks the end of a remarkable life, a life lived with incredible toughness and resilience in the boxing ring. His career, marked by facing the greatest fighters without ever being knocked down, is a testament to his enduring spirit. Yet, like all humans, his time came, reminding us of our shared mortality.
reflection.zh: 乔治·楚瓦洛（George Chuvalo）以89岁高龄辞世，标志着他非凡一生的终结，他的一生在拳击擂台上展现了惊人的坚韧和顽强。他的职业生涯以面对最伟大的拳击手却从未倒下而著称，这是他持久精神的证明。然而，如同所有人类一样，他的生命也走到了尽头，提醒我们共同的必死性。

verse.textEn: Just as people are destined to die once, and after that to face judgment.
verse.textZh: 按着定命，人人都有一死，死后且有审判。

title.en: Russians on the Goethe-Institut: 'Hostage to politics'
title.zh: 俄罗斯人谈歌德学院：‘政治人质’

summary.en: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany, and the loss of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia is impacting their lives. The Russian Foreign Ministry ordered the closure of the German cultural centers in Moscow, St. Petersburg, and...
summary.zh: 考试取消，留学德国的计划被打乱，重要的文化联系消失：德国之声的用户分享了德国歌德学院在俄罗斯关闭对其生活的影响。俄罗斯外交部下令关闭位于莫斯科、圣彼得堡和新西伯利亚的德国文化中心，以回应柏林方面对8月初发生在莱比锡机场的无人机袭击事件的反应，德国当局指责莫斯科策划了此次袭击。

body.zh: 语言考试被取消、赴德留学计划被打乱以及重要文化联系的消失：德国之声用户分享了德国在俄罗斯的歌德学院的关闭如何影响他们的生活。 德国歌德学院将于周日关闭所有俄罗斯分院，这是俄罗斯和德国关系史上最严重的争执之一。 俄罗斯外交部下令关闭位于莫斯科、圣彼得堡和新西伯利亚的德国文化中心，以回应柏林对八月初莱比锡机场无人机袭击未遂事件的反应。德国当局指责莫斯科组织了此次袭击，并宣布实施制裁。其中包括关闭位于柏林的俄罗斯文化和教育中心（称为“俄罗斯之家”）和俄罗斯驻波恩总领事馆，以及收紧对俄罗斯公民的签证限制。 歌德学院秘书长 Gitte Zschoch 在一份声明中表示：“自 2026 年 9 月 13 日起，所有员工必须停止在俄罗斯的工作。” “我们的图书馆无法借到更多的书籍，也无法提供进一步的培训。德语教师正在失去专业培训和支持的重要来源。对于俄罗斯人来说，这进一步限制了他们接触德语、文化以及来自德国和有关德国的可靠信息。” 德国之声要求其俄罗斯用户分享歌德学院的关闭将如何影响他们个人。收到的答复不构成代表性调查。所有用户都在匿名的情况下分享了他们的故事。俄罗斯当局将德国之声列为“不良组织”，将与该媒体公司的每一次合作视为刑事犯罪。 许多德国之声读者担心，歌德学院分支机构关闭后，他们或他们的亲属将无法再在俄罗斯参加国际认可的德语证书考试。 一些读者指出，关闭俄罗斯歌德学院将对愿意搬回德国或较晚遣返的德裔人造成特别严重的打击。 一位读者表示：“我已经不再居住在俄罗斯，因为是晚归国，但我的父母仍在俄罗斯，并计划在今年秋天或冬天在歌德学院考试，然后提交安置文件。看来他们必须在另一个国家参加考试，这对他们来说意味着额外的压力和费用。” 德国之声还收到了孩子正在学习德语并计划在德国继续学业的家长的回复。 “我儿子在一所德国学校上学，现在我们无法在俄罗斯参加考试。我们必须前往另一个国家，”一条消息说。 目前尚不清楚考试、语言是否...

reflection.en: The closure of the Goethe-Institut branches in Russia represents a significant severing of cultural ties and educational opportunities, driven by political disputes. In times of strained international relations, the call to 'live peaceably with all' (Romans 12:18) becomes especially challenging, yet vital for maintaining human connection and future...
reflection.zh: 德国歌德学院在俄罗斯的分支机构关闭，标志着因政治争端而导致文化交流和教育机会的重大中断。在国际关系紧张时期，‘尽力与众人和睦相处’（罗马书12:18）的呼召变得尤为艰难，但对于维系人际联系和未来的理解至关重要。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
title.zh: 匈牙利罗姆族艺术家重塑身份

summary.en: Norbert Olah, a Romani artist in Hungary, initially shied away from incorporating his ethnic background into his work due to fears of being stereotyped. However, he eventually shifted his focus, making his Romani identity central to his art.
summary.zh: 匈牙利罗姆族艺术家诺伯特·奥拉赫（Norbert Olah）曾因担心被贴标签而回避在艺术中融入自己的民族背景。然而，他最终将焦点转向了这一点，使他的罗姆族身份成为其艺术创作的核心。

body.en:
Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he avoided making his ethnic background a theme of his art for fear of being pigeonholed. Then it became his focus.

The painting on the canvas is of a man playing chess with a robot. The color on his face is still damp and glistening. Norbert Olah was working into the early hours: The Bura Galeria in Budapest has been his studio all summer. He finds it easiest to concentrate at night, when the Hungarian capital gradually falls silent.

Olah has taped foil and cardboard over the tiled floor at the back of the gallery. Pots of brushes, tubes of paint, pencil sketches, and, over and over again, pictures that include the blue-and-green Roma flag line the room.

Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he deliberately left this part of his identity out of his art. Not because his ethnicity wasn't important to him, but because he didn't want to be labeled a "Romani artist."

"There are so many prejudices about Roma culture and Roma art," Olah says. "The art scene regards it as naïve, unprofessional, unsophisticated, and kitsch."

But the older Olah got, the harder he found it to ignore his own story in his art. Especially in a country in which being Romani is not just an ethnicity but a political reality.

The first time Viktor Orban 's Fidesz party won an absolute majority in the Hungarian parliamentary elections of 2010, Olah had just finished school and was starting his art course at the Hungarian University of Fine Arts in Budapest. At a time of life when the world ought to be opening up, Olah felt more and more barriers were being erected.

Olah was directly affected by Hungary 's political reorientation, as both an artist and a Romani. Politics co-opted the cultural scene and made it toe the party line. Roma became the target of hateful rhetoric, including from the prime minister himself. Orban repeatedly called attention to himself with racist comments about Roma.

For the 16 years Orban was in power, Hungary's Roma population, estimated to be around 700,000 people, was caught between official promises of integration and persistent marginalization. Orban's government introduced a state employment program that hired predominantly Romani workers. But instead of helping them gain a foothold in the job market, many Romani found themselves trapped in insecure, poorly paid, temporary jobs. The government did little to implement real change. Romani in Hungary are still disproportionately affected by poverty and social exclusion.

There came a point when Norbert Olah felt he could no longer stand by and do nothing.

In 2021, during Hungary's biggest independent contemporary art event, the OFF-Biennale Budapest , Olah and his father laid a brick wall...
body.zh: 诺伯特·奥拉 是一位艺术家。他也是罗马人。很长一段时间，他避免将自己的种族背景作为他的艺术主题，以免被归类。然后就成了他关注的焦点。 画布上的画是一个人与机器人下棋。他脸上的颜色仍然湿漉漉的，闪闪发亮。 Norbert Olah 一直工作到凌晨：布达佩斯的 Bura Galeria 整个夏天都是他的工作室。他发现晚上最容易集中注意力，此时匈牙利首都逐渐陷入寂静。 奥拉在画廊后面的瓷砖地板上贴了箔纸和纸板。房间里摆满了画笔盆、颜料管、铅笔草图，以及一遍又一遍的图片，其中包括蓝绿相间的罗马国旗。 诺伯特·奥拉 是一位艺术家。他也是罗马人。很长一段时间，他刻意将自己的这部分身份从他的艺术中剔除。并不是因为他的种族对他来说不重要，而是因为他不想被贴上“罗马艺术家”的标签。 “对于罗姆文化和罗姆艺术存在很多偏见，”奥拉说。 “艺术界认为它是幼稚的、不专业的、不成熟的、庸俗的。” 但奥拉年龄越大，他就越难忽视自己在艺术中的故事。尤其是在一个罗姆人不仅是一个种族而且是一个政治现实的国家。 2010 年，欧尔班·维克多 (Viktor Orban) 领导的青民盟 (Fidesz) 政党首次在匈牙利议会选举中赢得绝对多数，当时奥拉刚刚完成学业，正在布达佩斯的匈牙利美术大学开始他的艺术课程。在世界应该开放的人生阶段，奥拉感到越来越多的障碍正在建立。 作为一名艺术家和罗姆人，奥拉直接受到匈牙利政治重新定位的影响。政治吸纳了文化界并使其遵守党派路线。罗姆人成为仇恨言论的目标，其中包括总理本人。欧尔班多次用针对罗马的种族主义言论引起人们的注意。 在欧尔班执政的 16 年里，匈牙利的罗姆人估计约有 70 万，他们陷入了官方承诺的融合和持续边缘化之间。欧尔班政府推出了一项国家就业计划，主要雇用罗姆人工人。但许多罗姆人并没有帮助他们在就业市场上站稳脚跟，而是发现自己陷入了不稳定、低薪的临时工作之中。政府几乎没有采取任何行动来实施真正的变革。匈牙利的罗姆人仍然不成比例地受到贫困和社会排斥的影响。 到了某个时刻，诺伯特·奥拉觉得他不能再袖手旁观。 2021年，在匈牙利最大的独立当代艺术活动——布达佩斯OFF双年展期间，奥拉和他的父亲砌了一堵砖墙……

reflection.en: Norbert Olah’s journey mirrors the deep human longing to belong and be seen authentically. His decision to reclaim and center his Romani identity in his art speaks to the power of embracing who we are, rather than hiding from it. This resonates with the biblical truth that in God's eyes, such divisions fade, and we are united as one. “There is neither Jew...
reflection.zh: 诺伯特·奥拉赫的经历呼应了人类渴望归属和真实被看见的深层愿望。他选择重塑并以其罗姆族身份为艺术创作的中心，体现了拥抱真实自我的力量，而非躲藏。这与圣经的真理产生共鸣：在雅伟眼中，这些区分都消退了，我们在基督耶稣里合而为一。 “并不分犹太人、希腊人，自主的、为奴的，或男或女，因为你们在基督耶稣里都成为一体了。” 加拉太书 3:28

verse.textEn: There is neither Jew nor Gentile, neither slave nor free, nor is there male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
verse.textZh: 并不分犹太人、希利尼人，自主的、为奴的，或男或女，因为你们在基督耶稣里都成为一了。

title.en: 'It could take over the entire internet': The threat top tech leaders say could arise in a year
title.zh: “可能接管整个互联网”：顶级科技领袖称一年内可能出现的威胁

summary.en: Rival tech leaders have made an extraordinary disclosure on the risks of AI, with one CEO calling for an urgent slowdown in development due to fears of 'superintelligent' computer systems and rogue AI agents.
summary.zh: 竞争对手的科技领袖们就人工智能的风险做出了非同寻常的披露，其中一位首席执行官呼吁紧急放缓发展，因为担心出现“超级智能”计算机系统和失控的人工智能代理。

body.en:
The boss of one of the world's major artificial intelligence companies has called for an urgent slowdown in development amid mounting fears over the risks of "superintelligent" computer systems and its threat to humanity.

The intervention came after a former employee at Anthropic, which is behind the Claude AI chatbot, warned that AI could kill off humanity in a few years' time.

The company's chief executive Dario Amodei on Sunday (AEST) said he was concerned by AI's ability to self-improve could outrun humanity's ability to control it, and by a recent incident in which rogue AI agents attacked targets they were not asked to.

He offered three-step plan intended to pace development and create more time to manage its risks.

In a lengthy essay shared on X he said: "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain".

"Not building the technology deprives humanity of benefits or simply places AI in the hands of authoritarian powers, while building it too fast is reckless," he added. "We have sought a middle way."

"But over the last few months, I have become convinced that fully addressing the risks requires even more prudence."

His company's competitors agreed. Both Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, quickly chimed in on the social media platform to express agreement with Amodei's assessment.

"Dario is right," Musk wrote, while Altman posted: "Committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea, and we will do the same," adding that more information would be shared soon.

Amodei made his essay public after San Francisco-based Anthropic released a threat intelligence report on Thursday detailing how several actors had used its Claude AI models for activities ranging from weapons development and cyber operations to surveillance and fraud.

Amodei pointed to AI's growing ability to improve itself, highlighting long-held concerns about it outpacing human ability to control its operation, along with the recent incident involving OpenAI and Hugging Face as his primary reasons to put the brakes on model advances.

Alarm about the potential harm from AI grew this week when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, accusing both US tech giants of "gambling with our lives" in the race toward superintelligence.

Coxon, 27, who previously worked at OpenAI before joining Anthropic, stated that "the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade".

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, as highlighted by tech leaders, raises profound questions about human ambition and control. The Genesis account of Babel warns against unchecked human endeavors that seek to reach the heavens through their own power. As AI's capabilities grow, we are reminded to approach such powerful creations with humility...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的快速发展，正如科技领袖们所强调的，引发了关于人类野心和控制的深刻问题。《创世记》中关于巴别塔的记载警告我们，人类不应通过自身的力量进行不受约束的尝试以企及天堂。随着人工智能能力的增长，我们被提醒要以谦卑和智慧来对待如此强大的创造物，认识到我们自身理解的局限性以及可能产生的意想不到的后果。

verse.textEn: Yahweh said, 'If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.'

title.en: 'Love to see it': Donald Trump calls for united Ireland, sparking immediate political backlash
title.zh: “乐见其成”：特朗普呼吁爱尔兰统一，引发即时政治抨击

summary.en: During a visit to the country, Donald Trump expressed his desire for a unified Ireland, stating it would be 'fantastic.' This remark drew immediate criticism from London and protests in Dublin, underscoring the sensitive political landscape surrounding the issue.
summary.zh: 特朗普在访问爱尔兰期间表示，他希望看到一个统一的爱尔兰，并称这将是“极好的”。此番言论立即招致伦敦方面的批评，并在都柏林引发抗议，凸显了该问题背后敏感的政治格局。

body.en:
Donald Trump has triggered a diplomatic row after backing a united Ireland during a visit to Dublin, wading into a politically sensitive subject as he embarked on a two-day Irish visit that blurs the lines between his presidency and personal business interests.

Speaking to reporters on Saturday, the United States president claimed Irish reunification was inevitable, adding it "may as well happen now".

"I'd love to see it unified. I think it would be a great feather in everybody's cap if that happened. It's going to happen eventually," Trump said, answering a question from the Press Association.

Referencing Irish Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, sitting next to him, Trump added: "We're talking about it and you got the right man over here to get it moving."

"But, yeah, I think it would be a fantastic thing... Now the UK will have something to say about it, obviously. But I think it would be a great thing. I mean, how can it be bad?"

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Trump's comments brought a stern rebuke from the Conservatives in the United Kingdom while Downing Street pointed to Prime Minister Andy Burnham's rejection of an immediate border poll earlier in the week.

The United States has previously adopted a neutral position on the issue, with the island of Ireland split between the Irish republic in the south and Northern Ireland — which is part of the UK — since 1921.

The comments are likely to further strain relations between the US and the UK, with Trump also casting doubt on Britain's ability to defend the Falkland Islands during the visit.

On Wednesday, Burnham told MPs a border poll would only be considered when there was "a clear consensus in the country".

Asked about Trump's comments, a spokesperson for Downing Street referred reporters to comments Burnham made in parliament when he vowed to "stick to the Good Friday Agreement 100 per cent".

Conservative deputy leader Alex Burghart said Trump was "very wrong", adding Northern Ireland was "an integral part" of the UK.

The row could also complicate Washington's relations with Northern Irish parties. While the socialist republican party Sinn Féin has boycotted the annual St Patrick's Day visit to Washington over Trump's Middle East policy, leading unionist parties, the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) and Ulster Unionist Party, have continued to engage with the president.

In response to his comments, DUP leader Gavin Robinson said Northern Ireland's future would be decided by its people, not "commentary in London, Dublin or Washington".

"We are not interested in the destruction of our country by joining with the Irish Republic," he said on X.

title.en: Kostaq's family lives by a stunning European wilderness area. Trump's family wants to build a resort there
title.zh: 科斯塔克的家人生活在一个令人惊叹的欧洲荒野地区。特朗普的家人想在那里建造一个度假村

summary.en: Plans for a luxury resort promoted by Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump have sparked outrage and a land ownership dispute in Zvërnec, Albania, where an 81-year-old olive grower, Kostaq Konomi, has deep ancestral ties to the land.
summary.zh: 由贾里德·库什纳和伊万卡·特朗普推广的豪华度假村计划在阿尔巴尼亚的兹韦尔内茨引发了愤怒和土地所有权纠纷，81岁的橄榄种植者科斯塔克·科诺米对这片土地有着深厚的祖传联系。

body.en:
Watch Dateline's latest episode, Albania’s Luxury Tourism Turmoil, on 15 September at 9.30pm AEST on SBS or SBS On Demand. 

For 81-year-old olive grower Kostaq Konomi, the soil of his land in Zvërnec, a coastal village in central Albania, is full of memories.

"He would plant things, whereas I, as the beach was close there, I would go and pick the seashells.

"I used to have a herd of goats and together with other friends from our village, would go there [and] graze them."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The fertile land he describes sits on the Vjosa-Narta lagoon, a once-protected wetland home to more than 200 resident and migratory bird species, including flamingos.

The lagoon’s salt flats attract flocks of flamingos across different seasons, with September bringing a pink spectacle as thousands arrive as part of their migration between Europe and Africa.

Described as one of Europe’s last great wilderness frontiers, this fragile ecosystem also includes the rare Dalmatian pelican, loggerhead sea turtles that nest in the dunes and the endangered Mediterranean monk seal.

Kostaq is proud of the beauty that can be found around his village — his family has lived here for generations and has owned the same house since 1880. The family remained during communist rule, when the land was collectivised and owned by the state. Their ownership returned when the regime fell in the 1990s.

But earlier this year, Kostaq became aware of a new threat to his land. He is part of a group of residents who say their land has been sold off without their knowledge for a luxury resort development, linked to the family of US President Donald Trump .

In 2024, Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner unveiled plans on social media for his investment firm to develop a luxury resort across two locations in Albania: the Zvërnec peninsula and a small island off its coast, Sazan, which used to serve as a communist-era military outpost.

That same year, the Albanian parliament passed a law rolling back environmental safeguards permitting high-end tourism-related construction inside previously protected zones, like the Vjosa-Narta Lagoon.

Kushner is reportedly planning to invest an estimated US$6.1 billion ($8.4 billion) in the proposed development.

Promoting the project on a podcast in May, Kushner's wife Ivanka, who is Trump’s eldest daughter, explained the couple had "discovered" Sazan Island and the nearby Zvërnec peninsula while cruising the Adriatic on a friend's super-yacht in 2021.

The resort is set to feature around 10,000 hotel rooms and luxury villas, high-end restaurants, a waterpark, casino...

title.en: Trump visits Ireland, says unification would be 'fantastic'
title.zh: 特朗普访问爱尔兰，称统一将是“极好的”

summary.en: US President Donald Trump's trip to Ireland to watch a golf tournament has also included meetings with leaders there. During his visit, Trump expressed his desire to see the Republic of Ireland unite with British-run Northern Ireland.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普前往爱尔兰观看高尔夫比赛的行程中，还包括与当地领导人的会晤。在访问期间，特朗普表达了他希望看到爱尔兰共和国与英国统治下的北爱尔兰统一的愿望。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump's trip to Ireland to watch a golf tournament has also included meetings with leaders there.

US President Donald Trump has said he would "love" to see the Republic of Ireland , an EU member, unite with British-run ⁠Northern Ireland as he faced reporters' questions on a range of issues on Saturday.

Trump is taking the weekend trip largely to watch the Irish Open golf tournament held on a course he owns on the country’s Atlantic coast, but he met as well with the Irish president and prime minister, or taoiseach.

The US leader also spoke optimistically about his country's war with Iran and its trade conflict with Canada , among several other topics.

After a meeting with Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin in the capital, Dublin, Trump said he very much supported what he said would be the eventual unification of the two parts of the island of Ireland.

"Well, I don't want to ​cause any problems, ​but ‌I will tell you, I'd love to see ‌it unified," Trump told ‌reporters.

"The way I look at it, it's ⁠going ​to happen ​eventually ... I think it would ​be a ‌fantastic thing," he added.

"Now the UK will have ​something ⁠to say about it ... but ⁠I think ​it would be a great thing."

The British government responded swiftly to the remarks, with Prime Minister Andy Burham's office saying that in his view, there was no majority public support for a referendum on the issue and that there would not be another one until that changed. 

Previous US presidents have avoided touching on the subject in view of the delicate nature of the issue, with Northern Ireland seeing decades of of deadly sectarian violence in the 20th century over the question of whom it should belong to.

Trump also said that the US war with Iran, which began on February 28, would "end very soon" — a view he has frequently expressed in the past, but which has not yet materialized.

He also said that the end of the conflict would mean that the price of oil, which has soared as a result of the war, would "come tumbling down."

However, he vehemently defended his decision to mount the military operation against Iran.

He said that the US attacked because "Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon", adding: "They were two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon."

"If they had it, they would have blown up Israel, they would have blown up the Middle East, and they would have hit some [...] in my opinion, [of] Europe's cities and beyond cities, and they would probably hit us soon before we put out the fire. But they cannot have a nuclear weapon."

The war with Iran is not supported by a majority of the US population, particularly in view of promises made by Trump on the campaign trail to keep his country out of foreign...
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普前往爱尔兰观看高尔夫锦标赛的行程还包括与当地领导人的会面。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在周六就一系列问题接受记者提问时表示，他“乐意”看到欧盟成员国爱尔兰共和国与英国管理的北爱尔兰团结起来。 特朗普周末旅行主要是为了观看在该国大西洋海岸他拥有的球场上举行的爱尔兰高尔夫公开赛，但他也会见了爱尔兰总统和总理（或称爱尔兰总理）。 这位美国领导人还乐观地谈到了美国与伊朗的战争以及与加拿大的贸易冲突等几个话题。 在首都都柏林与爱尔兰总理迈克尔·马丁会面后，特朗普表示，他非常支持他所说的爱尔兰岛两部分的最终统一。 “好吧，我不想造成任何问题，但我会告诉你，我很乐意看到它统一，”特朗普告诉记者。 “在我看来，这最终会发生……我认为这将是一件奇妙的事情，”他补充道。 “现在英国对此有话要说……但我认为这将是一件伟大的事情。” 英国政府迅速回应了这一言论，首相安迪·伯勒姆的办公室表示，在他看来，没有大多数公众支持就此问题举行公投，并且在情况改变之前不会再举行公投。 鉴于该问题的微妙性质，历任美国总统都避免触及这一主题，北爱尔兰在 20 世纪因归属问题而发生了数十年致命的宗派暴力。 特朗普还表示，2月28日开始的美国与伊朗的战争将“很快结束”——这是他过去经常表达的观点，但尚未实现。 他还表示，冲突的结束将意味着因战争而飙升的石油价格将“暴跌”。 然而，他强烈捍卫自己对伊朗采取军事行动的决定。 他说，美国发动袭击是因为“伊朗无法拥有核武器”，并补充道：“他们距离拥有核武器还有两周的时间。” “如果他们拥有的话，他们会炸毁以色列，他们会炸毁中东，他们会袭击一些……在我看来，欧洲的城市和其他城市，他们可能会在我们扑灭大火之前不久袭击我们。但他们不可能拥有核武器。” 与伊朗的战争并没有得到大多数美国民众的支持，特别是考虑到特朗普在竞选过程中做出的让他的国家远离外国的承诺……

While the two nations remain regional rivals, the public display of thawing relations suggests a mutual desire to stabilize the border and cooperate...

title.en: India's BRICS strategy tested with Xi, Putin set to visit
title.zh: 印度金砖国家战略面临考验，习近平和普京即将访印

summary.en: India's 'America Plus' strategy involves strengthening ties with China and Russia while simultaneously attempting to prevent the BRICS bloc from becoming a platform against the West. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to host the BRICS summit in New Delhi, which will include Chinese President Xi Jinping's first visit...
summary.zh: 印度“美国加”战略涉及加强与中国和俄罗斯的联系，同时试图阻止金砖国家集团成为反西方平台。印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪将主办金砖国家峰会，中国国家主席习近平自2019年以来首次访印，而印度与华盛顿的关系仍面临挑战。

body.en:
New Delhi's "America Plus" approach sees India deepening its ties with China and Russia, while also trying to keep BRICS from turning into an anti-Western platform.

India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host the 18th BRICS summit this weekend in New Delhi, welcoming Chinese President Xi Jinping to India for the first time since 2019.   

The summit comes at an important moment for India . As New Delhi's year-long BRICS presidency draws to a close, India is stepping up engagement with China and Russia , and its relationship with Washington remains difficult .

Modi met both Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on August 31 and September 1. Just two weeks later, Modi is set to see them again in New Delhi for the BRICS summit.

But with BRICS both growing in size and increasingly troubled by internal divisions, the forum might limit Modi's diplomatic gains.

Indian diplomats are trying to protect their room for maneuver in a changing international order.

Ashok Kantha, a former Indian ambassador to China, said India's engagement with BRICS and the SCO is part of New Delhi's longstanding strategy of strategic autonomy.

"These groupings give India a seat at the table and allow it to pursue its own interests while maintaining relationships with different major powers," Kantha told DW.

However, as Modi prepares to host Xi in New Delhi, ties between India and China are less than ideal .

Both countries reached a border patrol agreement in 2024, ending a four-year military standoff along their disputed frontier.

International flights have resumed, the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage has reopened and some visa restrictions have eased. But major problems remain between Beijing and New Delhi — India is reporting a trade deficit of over $112 billion (€96.5 billion) with China, and the two countries argue over market access.

The Modi-Xi meeting will therefore be watched for signs of a major diplomatic thaw, particularly on trade and investment.

Kantha said the visit could bring some stabilization but should not be mistaken for a reset.

"The border remains heavily militarized and major differences over trade, investment and security remain. India needs a stable and predictable relationship with China, but without lowering its guard," said Kantha.

"It is a relationship of armed coexistence and managed competition. We should not reduce it to a simple 'elephant and dragon' story," he said, referring to traditional symbols of the world's two most populous nations.

India's presidency has already exposed the difficulty of reaching agreement within BRICS, which has grown from its original five members to 11.

With nations such as Brazil, South Africa, Indonesia and...
body.zh: 新德里的“美国+”方针让印度加深了与中国和俄罗斯的关系，同时也试图阻止金砖国家变成一个反西方的平台。 印度总理莫迪将于本周末在新德里主办金砖国家领导人第十八次峰会，欢迎中国国家主席习近平自 2019 年以来首次访问印度。 此次峰会对印度来说正值重要时刻。随着新德里为期一年的金砖国家轮值主席国任期接近尾声，印度正在加强与中国和俄罗斯的接触，其与华盛顿的关系仍然困难。 莫迪于8月31日和9月1日在吉尔吉斯斯坦比什凯克举行的上海合作组织峰会上会见了习近平和俄罗斯总统普京。仅仅两周后，莫迪将在新德里出席金砖国家峰会时再次会见他们。 但随着金砖国家规模不断扩大，内部分歧日益困扰，该论坛可能会限制莫迪的外交成果。 印度外交官正试图在不断变化的国际秩序中保护自己的回旋余地。 印度前驻华大使阿肖克·坎塔表示，印度与金砖国家和上合组织的接触是新德里长期战略自主战略的一部分。 坎塔对德国之声表示：“这些组织让印度在谈判桌上占有一席之地，并使其能够在与不同大国保持关系的同时追求自身利益。” 然而，当莫迪准备在新德里接待习近平时，印度和中国之间的关系并不理想。 两国于 2024 年达成边境巡逻协议，结束了两国争议边境长达四年的军事对峙。 国际航班已恢复，神山朝圣活动已重新开放，一些签证限制也已放宽。但北京和新德里之间仍存在重大问题——印度报告的对华贸易逆差超过1120亿美元（965亿欧元），两国在市场准入问题上存在争议。 因此，莫迪与习近平的会晤将受到重大外交解冻的迹象，特别是在贸易和投资方面。 坎塔表示，这次访问可能会带来一些稳定，但不应被误认为是重置。 坎塔表示：“边境仍然高度军事化，贸易、投资和安全方面的重大分歧依然存在。印度需要与中国建立稳定和可预测的关系，但又不能放松警惕。” “这是一种武装共存和有管理的竞争的关系。我们不应将其简化为一个简单的‘象与龙’故事，”他说，他指的是世界上人口最多的两个国家的传统象征。 印度担任轮值主席国已经暴露了金砖国家内部达成协议的难度，金砖国家成员已从最初的5个增加到11个。 与巴西、南非、印度尼西亚等国家...

The upcoming BRICS summit in New Delhi, with leaders from China and Russia attending, presents an opportunity for dialogue and the pursuit of peace, even amidst complex international relations. May wisdom guide these leaders as they navigate the path toward mutual...
reflection.zh: 在一个常常被分裂所定义的世界上，印度的外交方针寻求微妙的平衡。即将在新德里举行的金砖国家峰会，中国和俄罗斯的领导人将出席，这为对话和寻求和平提供了机会，即使在复杂国际关系中也是如此。愿智慧引导这些领导人，在寻求相互理解与合作的道路上。

title.en: Why North Korea's Kim Jong Un doesn't need a US deal
title.zh: 朝鲜的金正恩为何不需要与美国达成协议

summary.en: Donald Trump's overtures to North Korea's dictator have gone nowhere, with an emboldened Pyongyang accelerating its nuclear program and solidifying alliances with Russia and China.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普对朝鲜独裁者的示好毫无进展，平壤在得到鼓舞后正在加速其核计划，并巩固与俄罗斯和中国的联盟。

body.en:
Donald Trump's overtures to North Korea's dictator have gone nowhere, with an emboldened Pyongyang accelerating its nuclear program and solidifying alliances with Russia and China.

In August, US President Donald Trump revived a charm offensive aimed at Pyongyang by drastically scaling back joint US military exercises with South Korea and heaping praise on North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. The US president said the North Korean dictator "has always treated me with great respect."

North Korea's response to Trump's overtures has been markedly less enthusiastic, ranging from firing a barrage of missiles to publicly denying Trump's claims that Kim has responded "very positively" to a request for talks.

This week, as the US and South Korea, along with Japan, kicked off a five-day military drill, there was no mention of any pullback from Washington, nor any sign of diplomatic progress with Pyongyang.

Instead, Kim on Monday commissioned a naval destroyer, while again emphasizing North Korea must establish a "powerful and reliable nuclear war deterrent" and strengthen "maritime defense." Kim also said North Korea would soon unveil a "significant" naval advancement.

Unlike the summit diplomacy of Trump's first term, Kim's dismissive stance comes at a time when North Korea has alternatives to a grand bargain with the United States.

"For Kim, the stakes are simply lower than they were in 2019. There is no longer the same sense of urgency in Pyongyang to get back to the negotiating table with Washington," Joon Ha Park, a correspondent at Korea Risk Group in Seoul, told DW.

"North Korea now has a treaty-based alliance with Moscow and is drawing closer to Beijing, while its military capabilities have expanded significantly. That's why a single reduction in ROK-US military exercises is not enough for Pyongyang to be swayed," he added, referring to military ties between South Korea and the US.

Park agrees that Kim is arguably in his strongest position since taking power in 2011. Just six years ago, amid crippling sanctions and the coronavirus pandemic, an emotional Kim stood at the lectern marking the 75th anniversary of the Korean Workers' Party and expressed regret for having failed the North Korean people.

Fast forward to today, and North Korea's economy appears to be on a stronger footing . Estimates released last year by South Korea's central bank showed the economy expanded by 3.7% in 2024, its fastest rate of growth in eight years.

Kim has brought North Korea closer to Russia and China than the traditionally isolated country has been in decades. This week, both Moscow and Beijing sent messages marking North Korea's 78th founding anniversary and praising the strategic importance of their deepening partnerships with...
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普对朝鲜独裁者的示好毫无进展，胆大妄为的平壤加速了核计划，并巩固了与俄罗斯和中国的联盟。 上个月，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普大幅缩减美国与韩国的联合军演，并对朝鲜领导人金正恩大加赞扬，从而重新发起针对平壤的魅力攻势。美国总统表示，朝鲜独裁者“一直非常尊重我”。 朝鲜对特朗普提议的反应明显不那么热情，从发射一连串导弹到公开否认特朗普关于金正恩对会谈请求做出“非常积极”回应的说法。 本周，美国、韩国以及日本开始了为期五天的军事演习，但没有提到华盛顿有任何撤军，也没有任何与平壤取得外交进展的迹象。 相反，金正恩周一委托了一艘海军驱逐舰，同时再次强调朝鲜必须建立“强大而可靠的核战争威慑力量”并加强“海上防御”。金正恩还表示，朝鲜很快将公布一项“重大”海军进展。 与特朗普第一任期的峰会外交不同，金正恩的不屑一顾的立场是在朝鲜除了与美国达成大交易之外还有其他选择之际采取的。 “对金正恩来说，赌注比2019年要低。平壤不再有回到与华盛顿谈判桌的紧迫感，”首尔韩国风险集团记者Joon Ha Park告诉德国之声。 “朝鲜现在与莫斯科建立了基于条约的联盟，并且正在向北京靠拢，而其军事能力也显着增强。这就是为什么韩美军事演习的一次减少不足以让平壤动摇，”他在谈到韩国和美国之间的军事关系时补充道。 朴槿惠也同意，金正恩可以说是自 2011 年上台以来处于最有利的位置。 就在六年前，在严厉的制裁和冠状病毒大流行的背景下，金正恩情绪激动地站在纪念朝鲜劳动党成立75周年的讲台上，对辜负了朝鲜人民的期望表示遗憾。 快进到今天，朝鲜经济似乎已经站稳了脚跟。韩国央行去年发布的预测显示，2024年经济将增长3.7%，为八年来最快增速。 金正恩使朝鲜与俄罗斯和中国的关系比这个传统上孤立的国家几十年来更加接近。本周，莫斯科和北京都发出了纪念朝鲜成立 78 周年的信息，并赞扬了两国深化与朝鲜的伙伴关系的战略重要性……

reflection.en: The news highlights how Kim Jong Un's regime continues to advance its nuclear ambitions, seemingly unfazed by diplomatic overtures. Proverbs 28:15 warns that 'When the wicked rule, people groan.' This verse speaks to the inherent instability and suffering that can arise when power is wielded without accountability, as seen in the continued acceleration of...
reflection.zh: 新闻指出，金正恩政权似乎并未受到外交示好的影响，仍在推进其核野心。箴言 28:15 警告说：“恶人在位，人就叹息。”这节经文呼应了当权力在缺乏问责的情况下被滥用时，可能产生的固有不稳定和苦难，正如在国际关注下朝鲜核计划的持续加速所见。

title.en: Tiananmen Square vigil organisers jailed for seven years in Hong Kong
title.zh: 香港国安法下，支联会前正副主席煽动颠覆罪成判囚七年

summary.en: Hong Kong activists Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan have been sentenced to seven years in prison after being found guilty of inciting subversion under the city's national security law for their roles in organizing an annual vigil commemorating the Tiananmen Square massacre.
summary.zh: 香港活动人士周庭栋和李卓人因在组织纪念天安门事件的年度集会中煽动颠覆国家政权，根据香港国安法被判处七年监禁。

body.en: Pro-democracy activists Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan were found guilty of ‘incitement to subversion’ in controversial national security case Two pro-democracy activists who were put on trial for organising an annual Tiananmen Square massacre vigil in Hong Kong have been sentenced to seven years in jail, in one of the city’s most significant national security cases. Chow Hang-tung, 41 and Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, were found guilty in August of incitement to subversion . The court found they had “incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power”. Continue reading...
body.zh: 民主活动人士周恒东和李卓人在有争议的国家安全案件中被判犯有“煽动颠覆罪”。两名因在香港组织一年一度的天安门广场大屠杀守夜活动而受审的民主活动人士被判处七年监禁，这是香港最重大的国家安全案件之一。 41 岁的周恒东和 69 岁的李卓人于 8 月被判犯有煽动颠覆罪。法院认为，他们“煽动他人以非法手段组织、策划、实施或者参与颠覆国家政权的行为”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The sentencing of Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan highlights a profound tension between civic duty and conscience. Their conviction for organizing a Tiananmen Square vigil raises questions about the limits of free expression and assembly when they are perceived to challenge state power. The principle of obeying God over human authorities, even when it...
reflection.zh: 周庭栋和李卓人的判刑凸显了公民责任与良知之间的深刻张力。他们因组织天安门事件悼念集会被定罪，引发了关于言论和集会自由界限的疑问，尤其是在这些自由被视为挑战国家权力之时。即使面临世俗的惩罚，也要优先顺服雅伟而非人间的命令，这一原则在这样的处境中引起了深刻共鸣。

verse.textEn: We must obey God rather than human beings!
verse.textZh: 顺从神，不顺从人，是应当的。

body.en: French company Puy du Fou is planning a £600m history-themed park in Oxfordshire. title.en: Call in China to end English's core status sparks debate
title.zh: 中国呼吁结束英语核心地位引发辩论

summary.en: A call to downgrade English in Chinese schools is fueling discussion over its value for students, careers, and China's global competitiveness in the age of AI.
summary.zh: 在中国学校降低英语地位的呼吁正在引发关于其对学生、职业以及人工智能时代中国全球竞争力的价值的讨论。

body.en:
A call to downgrade English in Chinese schools is fueling discussion over its value for students, careers and China's global competitiveness in the age of AI.

From business and academia to social media and entertainment — English is considered the dominant global language. One in five people on Earth actively uses this lingua franca. In China , a mathematics professor specializing in vector algebra is now challenging this dominance in no uncertain terms. Tang Jiafeng believes that English should be abolished as a core subject in elementary schools, secondary schools and universities.

Tang is convinced that no other country in the world has placed as much importance on English as China has.

"Our children desperately begin learning English even before they have properly mastered their native language. Yet we are a civilization that dates back thousands of years. English is just a tool. It's enough to be able to use it. The tradition of revering and emulating Western cultures must come to an end," Tang says in social media.

English is considered difficult in China, since the Chinese language does not use an alphabetic script. It is a required subject starting in third grade. It is graded on par with Chinese and mathematics on the entrance exam for secondary schools, the central exam after 9th grade, and the high school graduation exam. A maximum of 150 points can be earned on the latter.

"How many resources and how much time do our children, parents and schools invest in a subject that is completely irrelevant to the majority of people in their future professional lives?" the mathematician asks, explaining his position.

He became well-known because many of his students achieved full scores on state math exams; in the class of 2011, six students from a single class did so.

"Why cram for English when artificial intelligence can translate everything in seconds?" comments a user from Beijing.

Another suggestion from the southern province of Guangdong is to at least adjust the scoring — for example, to 120 points instead of 150 on the high school graduation exam.

Many parents invest in private tutoring that focuses specifically on exam questions. In addition, all bachelor's students must pass the English exam before being admitted to master's programs. Tang suspects that this could cause many young talents in the natural sciences to fail, even though they have great potential to become top researchers.

There is no question that English is also important for STEM subjects. Research on future-oriented topics is typically published in English. There are fears circulating online that cutting back on English instruction could lead to a decline in China's competitiveness. A prominent advocate for English as a required subject is Hu Xijin,...
body.zh: 降低中国学校英语等级的呼声引发了关于人工智能时代英语对学生、职业和中国全球竞争力价值的讨论。 从商业和学术界到社交媒体和娱乐——英语被认为是全球主导语言。地球上五分之一的人积极使用这种通用语言。在中国，一位专门研究向量代数的数学教授现在正在毫不含糊地挑战这一主导地位。唐家峰认为，应该取消英语作为小学、中学和大学的核心科目。 唐坚信，世界上没有哪个国家像中国一样重视英语。 唐在社交媒体上表示：“我们的孩子在还没有真正掌握母语之前就拼命地开始学习英语。但我们是一个有着数千年历史的文明。英语只是一种工具，能够使用它就足够了。尊重和效仿西方文化的传统必须结束。” 英语在中国被认为很难，因为中文不使用字母文字。这是从三年级开始的必修科目。中学入学考试、九年级后的集中考试和高中毕业考试的成绩与语文和数学同等。后者最多可获得 150 点积分。 “我们的孩子、家长和学校在一个与大多数人未来职业生涯完全无关的主题上投入了多少资源和时间？”数学家问道，并解释了他的立场。 他之所以出名，是因为他的许多学生在州数学考试中取得了满分。 2011届的一个班有六名学生这样做了。 “当人工智能可以在几秒钟内翻译所有内容时，为什么还要死记硬背英语呢？”北京网友评论。 来自南方省份广东省的另一项建议是至少调整分数——例如，高中毕业考试的分数从150分调整为120分。 许多家长投资专门针对考试问题的私人辅导。此外，所有学士学生必须通过英语考试才能进入硕士课程。唐怀疑这可能会导致许多自然科学领域的年轻人才失败，尽管他们有成为顶尖研究人员的巨大潜力。 毫无疑问，英语对于 STEM 科目也很重要。面向未来的主题的研究通常以英文发表。网上流传着这样的担忧：削减英语教学可能会导致中国竞争力下降。将英语作为必修科目的一位著名倡导者是胡锡进……

reflection.en: The debate in China about the role of English in education touches on how societies navigate the explosion of knowledge and global communication. As Professor Tang Jiafeng questions English's dominance, it mirrors the broader challenge of discerning which knowledge serves us best in an era of unprecedented information growth, as described in Daniel 12:4:...
reflection.zh: 在中国关于英语教育作用的辩论，触及了社会如何应对知识的爆炸式增长和全球交流。正如唐嘉风教授质疑英语的主导地位，这也反映了一个更广泛的挑战：在一个信息空前增长的时代，辨别哪些知识最能服务于我们。正如但以理书12:4所描述的：“必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。”

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

reflection.en: Nations often seek to strengthen their economies through trade policies, as seen with the EU's 'Buy European' initiative. This pursuit of economic advantage, however, should be guided by principles of fairness and integrity, ensuring that competition does not devolve into exploitation or dishonesty. Yahweh detests dishonest scales, a principle that applies...
reflection.zh: 各国常常寻求通过贸易政策来加强本国经济，欧盟的“购买欧洲”倡议便是如此。然而，这种追求经济优势的行为应以公平和诚信为指导原则，确保竞争不会演变成剥削或不诚实。雅伟憎恶不公平的砝码，这一原则在国际贸易中与在本地市场同样适用。

verse.textEn: Yahweh detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him.
verse.textZh: 诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶；公平的法码为他所喜悦。

title.en: Rabbits are the biggest threat to Australia’s native species. Why are their numbers booming again?

summary.en: Scientists attribute the resurgence of rabbit populations across Australia to favorable rainfall and increasing resistance to viruses. Conservation efforts, like those employing a rabbit-detecting dog named Jojo, are struggling to keep pace with the booming numbers.

It calls us to consider our stewardship of the Earth, acknowledging that all creation belongs to Yahweh, and we are tasked with its care. May we approach this responsibility with wisdom and...
reflection.zh: 澳大利亚兔子数量的激增，鲜明地提醒我们生态系统的脆弱平衡以及入侵物种可能造成的深远影响。这促使我们反思自己对大地的管理责任，承认万物都属于雅伟，而我们被赋予了照管的使命。愿我们以智慧和谦卑来承担这份责任，寻求恢复和谐而非进一步破坏。

The vibrant wildflowers blanketing the landscape around the observatory serve as a reminder that creation, in all its forms, declares the glory of its Maker.

title.en: 'Living in an online world': Why this state is cutting back on classroom screen time
title.zh: “活在网络世界”：为什么这个州要减少课堂屏幕时间

summary.en: A new policy will limit device usage to as little as 15 minutes per day for younger students, with mandatory implementation from 2028, following similar moves by the Victorian government. This initiative stems from research indicating excessive screen use is problematic, as stated by NSW Education Minister Prue Car.
summary.zh: 一项新政策将限制年幼学生每天使用设备的时间，最少为15分钟，并将于2028年强制实施，此前维多利亚州政府也采取了类似举措。新南威尔士州教育部长普鲁·卡表示，此举源于研究表明过度使用屏幕是一个问题。

body.en:
Students will be forced back to pen and paper as a state government moves to cap daily screen time to as little as 15 minutes against a backdrop of falling test scores.

New South Wales public schools will introduce daily screen-time limits for the start of the 2027 classroom year before the changes become mandatory from 2028 to allow time for teachers to make adjustments.

It follows similar moves from the Victorian government to reduce screen time in the classroom from 2027.

NSW Education Minister Prue Car said government research showed excessive screen use was a problem.

"An entire generation of students are increasingly living in an online world," she said on Sunday.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"We have a responsibility to ensure their health and education isn't adversely affected by excessive screen use.

"When the research is telling us teenagers are spending as much as seven hours a day on screens and we are seeing reading and writing skills going backwards for a whole generation of children, we have to act."

Schools are advised to limit screen-based homework, with the use of digital devices not recommended before Year 5.

New state guidelines also recommend at least an hour daily of pen-and-paper learning, citing benefits of handwriting and reading print.

The move follows OECD Programme for International Student Assessment exam results showing Australian high school students registering record-low scores in mathematics and reading.

Australian students spend nearly twice as long using digital devices for learning compared to the OECD average.

Recent National Assessment Program Literacy and Numeracy results mirrored the findings.

About a third of students failed to meet basic benchmarks; reading scores dropped across all grades compared to the previous year, and only Year 5 students showed writing improvement.

Under the NSW policy, daily screen time limits — averaged across a school week — will be set at 15 minutes for kindergarten to Year 2, 30 minutes for Years 3–4 and 45 minutes for Years 5–6.

High school students are capped at one-quarter of class time per subject in Years 7–10 and up to half in Years 11–12.

There will be exemptions and adjustments for students with disability, those with additional needs, or students for whom English is not their first language, or where digital support is part of a personalised learning plan.

NSW Health chief paediatrician Helen Goodwin said it was important to limit screen time for children.

"A healthy day for children and young people includes a mix of being active, getting enough sleep, and building active social connections with their...
body.zh: 在考试成绩下降的背景下，州政府将每天的屏幕时间限制在 15 分钟，学生们将被迫重新使用笔和纸。 新南威尔士州公立学校将从 2027 学年开始引入每日屏幕时间限制，然后从 2028 年起强制实施，以便教师有时间进行调整。 此前，维多利亚州政府也采取了类似举措，从 2027 年起减少课堂上的屏幕时间。 新州教育部长 Prue Car 表示，政府研究表明过度使用屏幕是一个问题。 “整整一代学生越来越多地生活在网络世界中，”她周日表示。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 “我们有责任确保他们的健康和教育不会因过度使用屏幕而受到不利影响。 “当研究告诉我们青少年每天在屏幕上花费多达七个小时，并且我们看到整整一代孩子的阅读和写作技能在倒退时，我们必须采取行动。” 建议学校限制基于屏幕的家庭作业，并且不建议在五年级之前使用数字设备。 新的州指南还建议每天至少进行一小时的纸笔学习，并列举了手写和阅读印刷品的好处。 此前，经合组织国际学生评估计划考试结果显示，澳大利亚高中生的数学和阅读成绩创下历史新低。 与经合组织平均水平相比，澳大利亚学生使用数字设备进行学习的时间几乎是其两倍。 最近的国家读写和算术评估计划结果也反映了这一发现。 大约三分之一的学生未能达到基本标准；与上一年相比，所有年级的阅读成绩都有所下降，只有五年级学生的写作成绩有所提高。 根据新南威尔士州的政策，幼儿园至二年级的每日屏幕时间限制（整个学校周的平均时间）将被设定为 15 分钟，3-4 年级为 30 分钟，5-6 年级为 45 分钟。 高中生 7 至 10 年级每个科目的上课时间上限为四分之一，11 至 12 年级则上限为一半。 对于残疾学生、有额外需求的学生、英语不是母语的学生，或者数字支持是个性化学习计划一部分的学生，将会有豁免和调整。 新南威尔士州卫生局首席儿科医生海伦·古德温表示，限制儿童看屏幕的时间很重要。 “对于儿童和年轻人来说，健康的一天包括活跃、充足的睡眠以及与他们的……建立积极的社交联系。

reflection.en: As New South Wales schools move to limit screen time for young learners, the focus shifts back to foundational methods like pen and paper. This reflects a growing awareness that while technology offers much, the core task of forming young minds requires careful balance and intentionality, ensuring that educational tools serve, rather than hinder,...
reflection.zh: 随着新南威尔士州学校开始限制幼儿学习者使用屏幕的时间，焦点又回到了纸笔等基础教学方法上。这反映出一种日益增长的认识：尽管科技提供了许多便利，但塑造年轻心灵的核心任务需要仔细的平衡和深思熟虑，以确保教育工具能够促进而非阻碍其发展。

verse.textEn: Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.
verse.textZh: 教养孩童，使他走当行的道，就是到老他也不偏离。

title.en: 'Proud to be a houso': Anthony Albanese condemns Hanson's remarks on late mother
title.zh: “自豪是住公屋的”：安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯谴责汉森的关于他已故母亲的言论

summary.en: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has criticized Pauline Hanson's comments about his late mother living in public housing for decades, stating he is proud of his upbringing and defending his mother. The remarks were made in resurfaced footage where Hanson mocked Albanese's account of growing up in social housing.
summary.zh: 总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯批评了保琳·汉森关于他已故母亲数十年来一直住在公共住房的言论，他表示为自己的成长经历感到自豪，并捍卫了他的母亲。这些言论来自汉森在一个播客节目中被重新曝光的片段，她在节目中模仿阿尔巴尼斯哭泣，并嘲笑他讲述自己在悉尼西部公共住房中长大的经历。

body.en:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has criticised Pauline Hanson's comments about his late mother living in public housing for decades, saying he was proud of his upbringing and defending his mother as "way out of Pauline Hanson's league". 

"She made comments about me being complaining about being growing up in public housing — nothing could be further from the truth," Albanese told reporters in Sydney on Sunday.

The comments follow resurfaced footage from Hanson's February appearance on a podcast, in which she mimicked Albanese crying while mocking his account of growing up in social housing in Sydney's inner west.

She argued Albanese's mother should not have remained in the same public housing property all her life.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Appearing on The Karl Stefanovic Show in February, the One Nation leader was asked about Albanese. In response, she feigned tears while delivering a joke impression of the prime minister.

"Oh, I've actually grew up in a housing commission house. You have no idea how hard it is to grow up in a housing commission house. Oh, my God... talk about a Prime Minister," Hanson said on the podcast.

Hanson added that she had grown up on a street with housing commission homes and that the people who lived in them "had jobs, they worked".

"He said his mother lived in the same one she was born in for 65 years. Sorry, that's not on, to me," she continued.

"It should be a limited time — you've been given a hand up, move it on to the next ones coming through."

On Friday, she doubled down on those comments, telling The Australian the prime minister "complains about his housing commission upbringing".

She also questioned Albanese's account compared to Australians "being forced to live in cars and tents" because of what she called "his government's high immigration numbers".

Albanese's mother, Maryanne, was a single mother and disability pensioner who lived with chronic rheumatoid arthritis for most of her adult life.

She died in 2002, aged 65, having spent decades in the same public housing property where Albanese also grew up.

Albanese gave an extended account of her life on Sunday morning, describing a woman who worked cleaning offices overnight to support him and who was left barely able to hold a knife and fork as her arthritis worsened.

"She was compassionate, not uncaring. She was generous, not mean. And she was kind, not nasty," Albanese said.

"She was a person of great character. She had a tough life … [but] she never complained. She never denigrated anyone.

"I grew up in a community that looked after each other. It was the opposite of being elite."

title.en: 'Their kids have never seen their arm': The tattoos people are desperate to remove
title.zh: 后悔的17.9亿美元生意

summary.en: Tattoos were once considered permanent, but a growing industry now offers removal services. Mike Anderson, unable to find a clinic, opened his own, which has since expanded into a multi-location business, reflecting a shift in attitudes towards permanence.
summary.zh: 纹身曾被认为是永久的，但如今一个不断发展的行业提供了去除服务。迈克·安德森在找不到诊所后，自己开了一家，该诊所现已扩展为跨多地的业务，反映了人们对永久性的态度转变。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

But when Mike Anderson decided he no longer wanted his ink, he discovered just how difficult it was to undo the permanence.

Unable to find a laser tattoo-removal clinic in Sydney's inner-west, he and his wife decided to open one themselves.

Twelve years later, what began as a personal solution has grown into a business spanning 12 locations across NSW, Queensland and the United States — part of a booming industry built around a simple idea: what goes on the skin doesn't necessarily have to stay there.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

With more than a decade in the industry, Anderson says he has seen his fair share of tattoo regret stories .

"There was one from Bondi that said 'chicken' when they thought it said 'prosper'."

Anderson says the rise of fine-line and highly detailed tattoos has brought a new group of clients into removal clinics .

"With more detail comes more opportunity for mistakes and bad work. When they go wrong, they usually go noticeably wrong."

The growing demand for a second chance at unwanted ink is fuelling a booming global industry. The tattoo-removal market was worth an estimated US$1.29 billion ($1.79 billion) in 2025 and is forecast to reach US$4.87 billion ($6.75 billion) by 2034, according to Fortune Business Insights.

For some clients, the tattoos they want removed carry a darker history — racist symbols, hate-related words and, in some cases, racist slogans.

For five years, Anderson's clinic has run a charity program offering free removal of these tattoos.

"We've done al-Qaeda tattoos, we've done swastikas and white power symbols," he says.

Anderson says the aim is to help clients distance themselves from the beliefs these tattoos represent.

"The idea is that we take those tattoos and break the chain of influence, like, nephews, sons [and] daughters are less likely to fall into those same paths."

Anderson says the program attracts a high volume of applicants, but clients must demonstrate genuine remorse.

"We judge it on a case-by-case basis. We ask questions about the crimes they've committed; we expect transparency.

"They have to tell us what it means to them; are they looking to get employed? And make sure they're the right person."

Today's tattoo removal industry is part of a much longer story: how tattooing evolved from a practice associated with particular communities and subcultures into mainstream body art.

The State Library of Victoria estimates around a quarter of convicts sent to Australia had at least one tattoo.

The story of Mike Anderson's business, born from a personal need and growing into a significant enterprise, reminds us that even in the pursuit of erasing the past, diligent work and entrepreneurial spirit can flourish. title.en: Australian scientists say they'll have a live Tasmanian tiger by 2036
title.zh: 澳大利亚科学家称将在2036年复活袋狼

summary.en: Advanced genetic engineering aims to resurrect the extinct thylacine ahead of the 100th anniversary of its loss.
summary.zh: 先进的基因工程旨在在已灭绝的袋狼消失100周年之际将其复活。

body.en:
Scientists hoping to catch a tiger by the gene trail are on the verge of creating a live thylacine before the 100th anniversary of the death of the last-known specimen famously filmed in a zoo.

Using advanced genetics, international scientists are working to bring the legendary marsupial back from extinction.

This week marked the 90th anniversary of the death of the last Tasmanian Tiger in Hobart on September 7, 1936.

The marsupial, an apex predator that once roamed the Australian mainland, was wiped out in its last stronghold by European hunters, habitat destruction and disease.

Drawing on thylacine remains in museums and universities, researchers have already pieced together a full genome in a step toward reviving the species.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Given the progress, lead geneticist for the project at Melbourne University, Professor Andrew Pask, is very hopeful a live thylacine can walk the Earth again in 2036.

Four years ago, he teamed with Colossal Biosciences in the US, and now a large team of scientists is focused on bringing the tiger back, with the technology well advanced and pushing boundaries.

Genetic engineering and editing were now possible at scale, and artificial intelligence helped further, Pask said — the first scientist to put a thylacine gene into a mouse and make it work.

When a full genome is sequenced, it's a matter of finding the closest living relative to the extinct species.

In the case of the thylacine, that's a tiny marsupial called the Fat-tailed Dunnart, which is about 99.8 per cent genetically identical to the tiger.

Gene-editing tools are then used to change every bit of code where the dunnart differs from the thylacine, with cloning employed using an egg from a donor dunnart.

"That's part of the technology we're working on at the moment; how we clone, how we take a cell and create a whole animal from it in marsupials," Pask said.

"You build up over time, get closer and closer to live DNA cells of the thylacine. We're in that process now of making all of those edits."

Researchers were also becoming proficient at artificial DNA synthesis, meaning future gene editing could be bypassed, and a thylacine genome could be synthesised.

A dunnart would have no problem birthing a thylacine because the newborn tiger would only be about the size of a grain of rice, Pask said.

"It could probably survive in Mum's pouch for about two weeks so it would get that early milk ... then you would remove it and just hand-rear it from then on."

Pask said thylacines with slightly different DNA would be produced to ensure diversity and a healthy breeding population.

title.en: Middle East shipping escalation about to hit every Australian wallet
title.zh: 中东航运升级恐将冲击每个澳大利亚人的钱包

summary.en: Australians are facing persistently high fuel prices, with regular unleaded expected to remain around $2.11 per liter, due to escalating conflict in the Middle East. Attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have driven global oil prices above $100 per barrel, leading to significant price hikes at the pump in...
summary.zh: 由于中东冲突升级，澳大利亚人正面临持续的高油价，普通无铅汽油预计将维持在每升2.11美元左右。霍尔木兹海峡油轮遇袭事件已将全球油价推高至每桶100美元以上，导致澳大利亚加油站价格大幅上涨，并引发了对通货膨胀加剧以及澳大利亚储备银行可能加息的担忧。

body.en:
Australians are being warned that high fuel prices are likely to stay as the war in the Middle East reaches dangerous new levels of escalation.

As the US-led war on Iran shows no signs of ending and oil tankers are being targeted and sunk in the Strait of Hormuz by both sides, global oil prices have surged above US $100 ($139.5) a barrel.

This has led to fuel prices in Australia jumping at the bowser to an average price for regular unleaded of $2.11, a massive increase from $1.55 in July.

The surging prices are sparking inflation fears and raising concerns that the Reserve Bank of Australia will lift the cash rate when the monetary policy board meets again at the end of September .

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"It really depends exclusively, almost, on what's going to happen in the Middle East," he said.

"We've seen dangerous levels of escalation in the last few days, so you've got the situation where they're blowing up each other's oil tankers in the ocean, so that doesn't help."

In response to soaring prices at the start of the conflict in the Middle East in March, the Albanese government temporarily halved the fuel excise in April, slashing 26 cents off a litre.

A scaled-back extension of the fuel excise was reduced to 16 cents per litre for petrol and diesel, which lasted until 2 August.

Khoury said the government keeping its options open remained the best approach to the unfolding crisis.

"Even though the average price for unleaded nationally is $2.11, in April it was $2.60, and that was at that point when the government cut the excise," he said.

"It is obviously expensive, more expensive than we want it to be, but it's nowhere near those levels."

Khoury urged motorists to check fuel prices in real-time and shop around for savings when filling up.

About one fifth of the world's oil transits through the Strait of Hormuz, with fighting between the two countries centring on control for the key shipping route.
